title: Vesper and the Salt
premise: Coral Delacroix, the last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that records trades of impossible things—discovers entries in her ledgers that no one wrote: prayers being answered by old gods long thought dead. The king of Vesper has been bound to a crown that answers his wishes at a terrible price, and Coral's own guildmaster sold him to it decades ago. To save the kingdom, Coral must choose between exposing the guild's crimes (destroying the only family she has left) or letting the crown consume the king, and she ultimately burns the ledgers themselves, unbinding the god from its contract and freeing both king and guild at the cost of her own name in history.
about_author: E. M. Sandoval is a former archivist who spent six years cataloging maritime trade documents before turning to fiction full-time. They write from a coastal town where the fog rolls in early, and they insist the sea keeps better secrets than any archive.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Things
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. In the flooded archive beneath Vesper's harbor, Coral balances the guild's impossible accounts—traded memories, borrowed years—while hiding her own illegitimacy within the order. She finds a ledger page written in no hand she knows, recording a prayer answered. Emotional beat: quiet unease; the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. A drowned sailor walks into the guildhouse demanding his debt be honored—he traded his death for a message, and the message is a prayer. Guildmaster Oren dismisses it, but Coral recognizes the handwriting from the anomalous page. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve as Coral realizes the old gods are listening again.

chapters.title: An Audience of Salt
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Summoned to court to audit the royal treasury, Coral meets King Aldric and sees the crown feeding on him—each wish granted costs him a memory, and he is nearly empty. His daughter, Princess Isolde, suspects something and watches Coral closely. Emotional beat: horror and unexpected tenderness; Coral's duty begins pulling against her heart.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Confronting Oren with evidence, Coral learns the truth: forty years ago he brokered the crown's contract to save a dying prince—the boy who is now the king—and the guild has been paid in silence ever since. Oren orders her to falsify the records. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty and truth split cleanly down the middle.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: POV: Isolde. Isolde, having followed her own investigation, corners Coral in the palace library and offers an alliance: help me save my father, and I'll shield you from your guild. Coral lies about what she knows. Emotional beat: wary connection; two women each holding half a truth, testing whether trust is possible.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Following the contract's terms through the deep ledgers, Coral descends to the salt cathedral under the harbor and meets the thing wearing the crown's reflection—an old god starving since worship ended, kept alive only by the king's memories. It offers her a trade. Emotional beat: terrible sympathy; the monster is also a victim, and Coral understands bargains now.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV: Isolde. The god accelerates its claim on Aldric, and the king begins erasing Isolde from his memory mid-conversation. Oren discovers Coral's copied pages and expels her from the guild, seizing her work. Emotional beat: grief and fury; everything Coral built her identity on is taken in a single night.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Cast out but not broken, Coral and Isolde gather the witnesses the guild wronged over a century—the drowned sailor among them—to build a case no court will hear. They plan to void the contract publicly, forcing the god into open negotiation rather than secret consumption. Emotional beat: defiant hope; justice assembled from the discarded.

chapters.title: The Reading of Accounts
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. In the throne room before the assembled court, Coral reads the true ledger aloud—every crime, every payment, Oren's original bargain—as the god manifests through the crown to defend its claim. When negotiation fails, Coral invokes the oldest clause: a ledger may be burned by its keeper, voiding all debts. Emotional beat: climax; courage at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Ash and Afterward
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Coral burns the ledgers, unbinding the god—which departs not in rage but in gratitude, finally released from hunger—and the king wakes whole if diminished. Oren faces the guild's reckoning; Coral, keeper of nothing now, chooses to stay and build something honest beside Isolde. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; love chosen freely, duty redefined.
